newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-BACHER BACKS CALLS FOR BIENNIAL WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BACHER BACKS CALLS FOR BIENNIAL WORLD CUP.

text.p: Ali Bacher, one of the world's senior cricket administrators, said on Sunday he was backing calls for the World Cup to be changed from a four-yearly tournament to a biennial event.

The recommendation is one of several that Bacher, managing director of the United Cricket Board of South Africa, has made in his role as chairman of the International Cricket Council (ICC) development committee and it comes just three weeks after the West Indies Cricket Board made a similar appeal.
With England hosting the seventh World Cup in 1999, Bacher said South Africa, and not the West Indies, would host the following edition, whether it was in 2001 or 2003.
"It has been confirmed that we (South Africa) have got the eighth World Cup," he said.
Bacher hopes the proposal to make the World Cup a two-yearly event will gain approval at the annual meeting of the full ICC in June.

"The most effective marketing tool to spread cricket and inspire the youth of the world to play the game is through internationally televised cricket. And the most formidable tool we have to do that is to hold the World Cup every two years," Bacher told Reuters.

Bacher also wants to see the number of teams competing in the World Cup increased from the current 12 to 16 for the eighth edition and leading ICC associate member countries to be given official one-day international status.

Other recommendations include setting up a world test cricket championship to preserve the five-day game's status and appointing regional development officers in the five major cricketing areas of the globe.
"When we talk about countries where cricket is a high profile sport it is actually a very small number," explained Bacher.
"We need to come up with a strategy to get the cricket message into new markets and increase the numbers of cricketers in existing markets where the game has a low profile.

"The World Cup is the way to do that. I know from speaking to government ministers in Kenya that cricket's profile was raised substantially by their country's participation in the 1996 World Cup and their historic win over the West Indies.
The extra revenue would be redirected back into development, he said.

The ICC development committee -- which includes West Indies vice-president Julian Hunte, MCC secretary Roger Knight and Pakistan's chief executive Majid Khan -- has discussed the interim report which has now been submitted to all member countries for consideration.
It will be discussed when they meet at the ICC Trophy in Malaysia on March 18 before a final report goes to the ICC annual conference in London in June.
